etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin sōlicitus, sollicitus (“thoroughly disturbed, anxious”), from sollus (“whole, entire”) + cieō (“move, disturb”). By surface analysis, solicit +‎ -ous.
senses: Disposed to solicit; eager to obtain something desirable, or to avoid anything evil.
(Usually followed by about, for, etc., or a clause) Showing care, concern, or attention, in any of several ways:
